# Row-level table property exceptions

Original controls generated by `tools/table_row_exceptions_fixture.py` using
python-docx and original OOXML. No corpus content or third-party renderer is
included. The reference application exported `controls-native.pdf` after
confirming the exact source path; the current source passes schema validation.

Sixteen cases occupy eighteen native pages: partial/all border overrides,
inside versus outer borders, none/nil, cell precedence, adjacent rows, horizontal
and vertical merges, first/last rows, per-row conditional-style look flags,
page-spanning merges and repeated headers. `cases.json` records their order.
The last two cases occupy two pages each.

Relevant clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.40 (table border exceptions), §17.4.55
(table look exceptions), §17.4.61–62 (table property exceptions). Cell borders
take precedence over row exceptions; omitted exception sides inherit table
borders. Interior horizontal edges use insideH. At a page cut, the reference application uses the
physical last row's outer bottom edge. Merged cells retain different vertical
border segments for their physical rows.

`tools/table_row_exceptions_reference.py` records the source/PDF hashes and
colored ink projections from the native PDF at 96 dpi. The anti-alias mask
accepts mixtures with white and restricts the palette to the colors used by
each case, preventing text over shading from matching an unrelated border
color. The browser regression compares every disconnected X/Y band within 1pt
before and after export/reopen, including short caps at merged-side transitions.
These are paint checks, in addition to matching pagination and edit round trips.
